questions.question: A power has base m and exponent 4. It is multiplied by another power with base m and exponent 2. Written as a single power, what is the product?
questions.explain: Same base, so keep m and add the exponents: 4 + 2 = 6, giving m⁶. Multiplying the exponents to get m⁸ is the common trap.

questions.question: A power with base 3 and exponent 2 is multiplied by a power with base 3 and exponent 5. Which single power equals the product?
questions.explain: Keep the base 3 and add the exponents: 2 + 5 = 7, so 3⁷. The bases are never added; 6⁷ is a completely different number.

questions.question: A power has base y and exponent 9. It is divided by a power with base y and exponent 3. Which single power is the quotient?
questions.explain: Dividing powers with the same base: keep y and subtract the exponents, 9 − 3 = 6, so y⁶. Do not divide or multiply the exponents.

questions.question: The number 2 is used as a factor 7 times, giving the power 2⁷. This is divided by 2⁴, where 2 is a factor 4 times. Write the quotient as a single power of 2.
questions.explain: 2⁷ ÷ 2⁴ keeps the base 2 and subtracts the exponents: 7 − 4 = 3, so 2³. The base stays 2; it is not divided by itself.

questions.question: Write n² × n⁴ × n³ as a single power.
questions.explain: All three powers share the base n, so add every exponent: 2 + 4 + 3 = 9, giving n⁹. The base is written once, never as 3n.

questions.question: A Kelowna lab counts 10⁴ bacteria in a dish. Overnight the count is multiplied by 10³. Written as a single power of 10, how many bacteria are there now?
questions.explain: 10⁴ × 10³ keeps base 10 and adds the exponents to give 10⁷. Multiplying the exponents (10¹²) or adding the bases (20⁷) are the usual errors.

questions.question: A rectangular poster has an area of 2¹⁰ cm² and a width of 2⁴ cm. Written as a power of 2, what is its length in cm?
questions.explain: Length = area ÷ width = 2¹⁰ ÷ 2⁴; keep base 2 and subtract the exponents to get 2⁶ (64 cm). Check: 2⁶ × 2⁴ = 2¹⁰.

questions.question: Simplify (k⁵ × k³) ÷ k² to a single power.
questions.explain: Multiply first by adding exponents (5 + 3 = 8), then divide by subtracting (8 − 2 = 6): k⁶. Multiplying 5 × 3 to get k¹⁵ at the first step leads to k¹³.

questions.question: Jordan writes 4³ × 4⁵ = 8⁸ and explains, 'you add the bases and add the exponents.' What is the correct single power, and why?
options: 4⁸, since only the exponents get added
8⁸, since the bases get added as well
8¹⁵, since bases add and exponents multiply
questions.explain: When powers with the same base are multiplied, the base is written once and only the exponents are added: 4³ × 4⁵ = 4⁸. Adding the bases to get 8⁸ changes the value completely.

questions.question: Each fold of a sheet of paper doubles its layers. Ava folds one sheet 3 times, so it has 2³ layers. She then stacks 2⁴ of these folded sheets on top of each other. How many paper layers are in the stack?
questions.explain: The stack has 2³ × 2⁴ layers; keep base 2 and add the exponents to get 2⁷ = 128. Multiplying the exponents (2¹²) or adding the bases (4⁷) gives far too many layers.

questions.question: An Okanagan farm has a crate of 5⁷ cherries. They are packed 5² cherries per bag, and then the bags are packed 5⁵ bags per box. How many boxes are filled?
questions.explain: 5⁷ ÷ 5² = 5⁵ bags, then 5⁵ ÷ 5⁵ = 5⁰. Any number divided by itself is 1, so 5⁰ = 1 box, not 0.

questions.question: A food drive in Victoria collects 2⁵ boxes, each holding 2⁴ cans. All the cans are shared equally among 2³ food banks. As a single power, how many cans does each food bank get?
questions.explain: Multiply by adding the exponents (2⁵ × 2⁴ = 2⁹), then divide by subtracting (2⁹ ÷ 2³ = 2⁶). Keep the base 2 the whole way; it never becomes 4.
